Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, General Plan Advisory Committee Members will be

839 7711 1001 Passcode: 092366 (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol  Corea, Administrative Assistant at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Committee Members for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”

you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Committee and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 839 7711 1001 Passcode: 092366

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  MOBILITY ELEMENT

The Committee Members participated in poll #1, as follows:

What is your preferred mode of travel? The multiple choice answers, included, 1. Driving alone;
2. Driving with friends, family, or co-workers; 3. Taking transit; 4. Walking; 5. Biking; 6. Riding my
horse; 7. It depends on what I’m doing.
The poll results showed that the preferred mode of travel is Driving.
Surabhi Barbhaya, MBI, began the meeting with the introduction of the team from Fehr & Peers.
John Muggridge, Fehr & Peers provided a recap of the areas that have been discussed, which
are unique to the City. They include, the rural feel and equestrian community; 8,200 residents;
topographical constraints; many older residents and young families. There are different
transporation needs in the community and this City is a car-centric environment. The Mobility
Element is not about forcing people out of their cars and rather providing options for people to get
around the City.
Mr. Muggridge provided data from the 2010-2014 American Community Survey, which shows that
many residents in the City work from home. More recent ACS statistics show that the percentage
of residents who work from home has decreased. However, working from home is still an
important part of life in the City and due to the pandemic it is more achievable, and will likely
continue.
Natalie Chyba, Fehr & Peers provided a review of the Mobility Element focused sections of the
Vision Statement and Guiding Principles.
The Committee Members participiated in poll #2, as follows:
How many topic areas (or “issues”) are included in Rolling Hills Estates’ current General Plan Mobility
Element? The multiple choise answers, included: 1. Three; 2. Six; 3. Ten.

The poll results and the correct number of topic areas in the City’s current General Plan Mobility
Element is six.

Ms. Chyba provided the existing Transportation Element “issues”, which include, Safe Driving
Conditions; Efficient Traffic Flow; Multi-Use Recreational Trails; Transit & Transportation Demand
Management; Parking Areas; and, Roadway Classification. Ms. Chyba stated that in looking how to
incorporate these into the 2040 Mobility Element, these are still relevant today. The 2040 Mobility
Element topics are proposed be updated as follows:

  •  (Existing) Safety Driving Conditions & Roadway Conditions = (Update) Transportation Network
  & Safe Street Design
  •  (Existing) Efficient Traffic Flow = (Update) Vehicular Circulation
  •  (Existing) Multi-Use Recreational Trails = (Update) Pedestrian Circulation & Recreation Trails
  and Bicycle Circulation
  •  (Existing) Transit & Transporation Demand Management = (Update) Transit & Transporation
  Demand Management

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, JANUARY 19, 2021
 Seth Contreras, Fehr & Peers, stated that each of these topic areas have been co-authored by the
GPAC, through Community Engagement, Best Practices and Peer City Review, and looking to Future
Trend Focus Areas.

Mr. Contreras provided an overview of each of the Mobility Element Topic areas, as follows:

  •  Transportation Network & Safe Street Design – emphasis is on safety
  •  Vehicular Circulation – car travel and addressing traffic
  •  Pedestrian Circulation – highlight sidewalks and create a walkable commercial district
  •  Recreation Trails & Bicycle Circulation – promote more policies on bike supporting
  infrastructure and also equestrian specific policies
  •  Transit & Transporation Demand Management – more transportation options for the
  community

Mr. Muggridge stated that one thing that ties the Mobility Element, Sustainability Element and Land
Use Element together is Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT). An overview of SB 743 CEQA key requirement
were presented, which include, Reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions (Sustainability);
Encouraging infill development (Land Use); and, Improving public health through increased active
transporation (Mobility).

The GPAC Members participated in “break-out” sessions to discuss the following topic areas:

  •  Group 1: Transport Network & Safe Street Design / Transit & Transit Demand Management
  •  Group 2: Vehicular Transporation
  •  Group 3: Circulation / Recreation Trails & Bicycle Circulation

6.  COMMITTEE ITEMS / FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

Due to the loss of quorum, the discussion will be continued at a future meeting.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the committee and adjourned the meeting at 6:58 p.m.
